title: Operating system installation and BIOS/UEFI

spans.caption: A diagram of the lesson’s key ideas

spans.text: Formatting a disk can erase files. Get the user’s approval, make a backup somewhere else, and verify that it opens. Confirm the license and recovery keys, power, correct device, and official installation source. Stop if there is no verified backup.

Use Microsoft’s official installation media or recovery option to reinstall Windows. Check the disk and partition carefully: deleting the wrong partition can destroy other data. On a company computer, do this only with authorization and the approved procedure.

Create installation media from the official website of the Linux distribution you chose. Check the keyboard, language, network, and disk selections in the installer. “Erase disk” can remove all data on that disk; choose it only after the backup, permission, and target disk are confirmed.

On a Mac, first back up with Time Machine or another organization-approved method. Start macOS Recovery for the specific model, and erase the disk and reinstall only when needed. Startup steps differ between Apple silicon and Intel models; follow Apple’s official instructions.

BIOS/UEFI checks hardware as a computer starts and helps load the operating system. UEFI is the modern firmware used by most current computers. Its setup menu can include the clock, boot order, and device options. The key to open it varies by manufacturer.

Change only a setting you understand and are authorized to change. Changing boot order or Secure Boot/TPM settings can require a disk recovery key or prevent startup. Record the original value first. Update BIOS/UEFI only with the manufacturer’s instructions and stable power.
